name: s3-protrusions-to-enclosure
title: S3 — Protrusions to enclosure: can protrusion mechanics reach stable wrapping?
concept: Compartmentalization made operational as the topology of enclosing membranes and the energy of deformation. Membrane geometry and mechanics parameterized from cryo-ET / live imaging; classical engulfment, inside-out wrapping, and a no-enclosure control compared.
question: Can observed archaeal protrusion mechanics plausibly transition from contact to stable wrapping / engulfment, within membrane area, bending-cost, and timescale budgets? Morphology alone cannot demonstrate engulfment.
hypothesis: Under cryo-ET-constrained bending moduli and observed protrusion timescales, at least one topology (classical engulfment or inside-out wrapping) reaches a stable enclosed state with conserved membrane area and a finite energy budget, while a no-enclosure control does not.
claim: Physical enclosure is a separate hurdle from metabolic benefit: observed protrusion mechanics can, under restricted geometry and bending-cost regimes, reach stable wrapping — but a beneficial symbiosis (S1/S2) need not imply ingestive ability, and some topologies never enclose within realistic area/energy budgets.

behavior_tests.name: enclosure-geometrically-feasible
behavior_tests.description: At least one topology reaches a stable enclosed state above a probability threshold.

provenance.note: Fraction of parameterized runs reaching stable enclosure; >0.5 within the cryo-ET-constrained regime. Priors from Rodrigues-Oliveira-2023 and Radler-2026.

behavior_tests.name: membrane-area-conserved
behavior_tests.description: Membrane area is conserved through the deformation (no area created from nothing).

literature_anchors.expectation: Cryo-ET constrains Asgard membrane morphology and actin-based structure.

baseline.name: baseline
baseline.note: Composite NOT yet built. Requires: a deformable-membrane mechanics process, cryo-ET-derived geometry priors, and an area/energy-budget validator; three arms (engulfment, inside-out, no-enclosure control).
